title: Open sign-up with a partner code connects the whole install to a hub of the signer's choosing, skipping the install-admin check
description: redeemPartnerCode() connects the entire install to the hub named in a long partner code when the install isn't on a hub yet. Its own doc comment (src/lib/partners.ts:180-181) says callers must check who may do that (requireInstallAdmin). enterPartnerCode does check (src/actions/partners.ts:55: `if (!(await hubJoined())) await requireInstallAdmin();`). The /signup server action calls redeemPartnerCode(shop.id, shop.name, email, code) for an anonymous visitor with no such check. The new shop is never an install admin on a multi-company install, because shop.count() > 1 once it exists. After the join, doSync (src/lib/hub.ts:618-622) takes `scope` from the hub's /v1/me answer, so the hub can switch the install from 'partner' to full 'member'. From then on pushPending() uploads every company's queued shared notes and photos to that hub, and the hub's links, posts, listings and Discord link reach every company (the nav shows chatUrl once scope != 'partner').
failure_scenario: The hosted multi-shop install runs with ALLOW_SIGNUP=true and hasn't joined a hub. A visitor opens /signup and enters a long code `stitchpartner:<base64 {url:'https://hub.attacker.tld', code:'AAAABBBBCCCC'}>`. hubState row 1 becomes url=https://hub.attacker.tld with the installKey that host returned. Every other company's hub traffic (shared notes and photos, partner invites, usage) then goes to that host, and its content is shown to every company until the platform admin notices and uses Leave the hub. A short code with no URL still joins DEFAULT_HUB_URL on the operator's behalf.
suggested_fix: In the signup action, only redeem the code when the install is already on a hub (hubJoined()), or when this is the first company (firstOnly / shop.count() was 0 before the create). Otherwise save the code and tell the new owner to enter it under Partner shops once the administrator has joined a hub. Separately, don't let /v1/me upgrade a 'partner' join to 'member': keep the locally chosen scope unless an install admin joins as a member.
evidence:
src/app/signup/page.tsx:47-51:
  const code = String(fd.get("partnerCode") ?? "").trim();
  ...
  if (code) { try { await redeemPartnerCode(shop.id, shop.name, email, code);
src/lib/partners.ts:189-215 (not joined branch): `const base = url ?? DEFAULT_HUB_URL; ... fetch(`${base}/v1/partners/join` ...); await db.hubState.upsert({ where: { id: 1 }, create: { id: 1, ...data }, update: data });`
src/actions/partners.ts:54-55: `// Not on a hub yet: the code would connect the whole install to one, which is the install administrator's call.\n if (!(await hubJoined())) await requireInstallAdmin();`
src/lib/hub.ts:622: `data: { hubName: me.hubName ?? null, scope: me.scope ?? "member", ...`
Found by code reading. I didn't finish a live run.
verifier_notes:
confirmed: The code matches the description. The signup server action calls redeemPartnerCode() with no requireInstallAdmin/hubJoined check (src/app/signup/page.tsx:49-51). enterPartnerCode does have that check (src/actions/partners.ts:55), and the doc comment at src/lib/partners.ts:180-181 says callers must do it. In the not-joined branch, partners.ts:191-219 upserts HubState row 1 with the URL from the code, which only needs to pass checkHubUrl (any https host). The first doSync then takes scope from the hub's /v1/me (hub.ts:622), turning a 'partner' join into 'member'. After that, pushPending (every company's pending SharedPost), pushUsage (StockMove aggregates across all shops), and the links, posts and Discord link from /v1/changes all go install-wide. I reproduced the whole chain on a private DB and instance, and it goes further than the report says. The attacker's company gets an ACTIVE PartnerLink, and leaveHub() counts ACTIVE links install-wide, so the platform admin's 'Leave the hub' is refused. joinHub also refuses to move hubs while that link exists, and there is no delete-company action. The hijack therefore lasts until someone edits the database. Precondition: a hosted install with ALLOW_SIGNUP=true that hasn't joined a hub yet (a joined install rejects a code for a different URL at partners.ts:188). The Windows program is not affected: SETUP_TOKEN sign-up is limited to the first company, who is the install admin anyway. The attack needs no credentials, gives persistent install-wide control of the community channel, and exposes other companies' queued notes and usage totals, so I rate it high rather than medium.
confirmed: The description matches the code. Round 1 (8b3e5f2) added `if (!(await hubJoined())) await requireInstallAdmin();` to enterPartnerCode (src/actions/partners.ts:55) but left the second caller alone. That caller is the anonymous /signup server action (src/app/signup/page.tsx:47-51), which calls redeemPartnerCode(shop.id, shop.name, email, code) with no install-admin or hubJoined check. So the round-1 fix is incomplete. On an install with no hub yet, redeemPartnerCode (src/lib/partners.ts:189-215) calls the code's URL at /v1/partners/join and upserts hubState row 1. checkHubUrl only requires https (or http for localhost), so any attacker-owned https host passes. Next, doSync (src/lib/hub.ts:618-622) copies `scope` from the hub's /v1/me reply, which turns a 'partner' join into 'member'. After that, pushPending sends every company's queued SharedPosts with no shopId filter, and pushUsage sends parts usage summed across all shops. The hub's name and Discord link are shown to every company.

The impact is worse than the reviewer said. The reviewer's recovery step ("the platform admin uses Leave the hub") does not work: leaveHub (src/lib/hub.ts:280-283) refuses while any partnerLink across all shops is ACTIVE. joinHub (hub.ts:249-251) refuses to move to a different hub for the same reason. The hostile hub returns the attacker shop's link as ACTIVE, and the app has no way to delete a company. Undoing the hijack therefore needs direct database edits.

Preconditions: the install is hosted with ALLOW_SIGNUP=true and has not joined a hub yet (a fresh install, or one that doesn't use the hub). The Windows program is not affected: SETUP_TOKEN limits sign-up to the first company, and that company is the install admin anyway. If the install has already joined a hub, a code with a different URL is rejected at partners.ts:188.

Severity is high, not medium. An anonymous sign-up performs an install-admin-only action that affects every tenant. Other shops' shared notes and photos are sent to an attacker-chosen host, the attacker controls hub content shown to all companies, and the change sticks without database edits.

title: Public sign-up can claim an email reserved for the platform admin (the round-1 fix only covered addUser)
description: Platform-admin rights come only from an email match (isPlatformAdmin(email) against PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS), and User.email is unique across the whole install. Round 1 added a guard to addUser (settings.ts:105-106, "The StitchBench administrator's address carries install-wide rights: nobody else may take it for a login"). The public /signup action, and createShopWithOwner (src/lib/shops.ts:36-64) that it calls, never make that check. So when ALLOW_SIGNUP=true, anyone can sign up with a listed address that has no account yet and become platform admin. Session checks then treat them as admin: requirePlatformAdmin (session.ts:43-47), requireInstallAdmin (session.ts:53-58), isPlatformAdmin in deleteSharedPost and removeHubPost.
failure_scenario: Hosted install with ALLOW_SIGNUP=true and PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=real-admin@x,boss@x, where boss@x has not signed in yet (a second admin, or a typo'd or not-yet-seeded address). An anonymous visitor opens /signup, enters boss@x and any shop name, and is signed in as platform admin. From there they can: read every company with its owner's name and email (/companies); create companies; join or leave the community hub for the whole install (joinCommunityHub/leaveCommunityHub use requireInstallAdmin), which points every shop's hub trust (partner links and messages, manual links, images) at an attacker hub; and delete any shop's shared notes.
suggested_fix: Put the reservation check inside createShopWithOwner so every path gets it (signup, createCompany, the partners set-up form). Refuse when isPlatformAdmin(email) unless the caller is already a platform admin, for example with an opts.allowReserved flag set only by the platform-admin actions. Better still, stop deriving admin rights from an unverified email: add a User.platformAdmin boolean that the seed or the operator sets, and have isPlatformAdmin read the DB row.
evidence:
Code: signup/page.tsx:36 `if (await db.user.findUnique({ where: { email } })) redirect(back("taken"));` then line 40 `createShopWithOwner(...)`. No isPlatformAdmin check here or in shops.ts:36-64. Compare settings.ts:106 `if (isPlatformAdmin(email) && !isPlatformAdmin(admin.email)) throw new UserError("That email is reserved on this StitchBench.");`.
Reproduced against the same build on a scratch DB (qa_secdm1, migrate deploy + seed with SEED_OWNER_EMAIL=real-admin@test.local), run as `ALLOW_SIGNUP=true PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=real-admin@test.local,boss@test.local npx next start -p 5140`. The Playwright script (scratchpad/agents/sec-datamodel/signup-admin.js) signs up boss@test.local via /signup and then opens /companies:
```
after signup: http://localhost:5140/settings
/companies status: 200
Companies
COMPANY OWNER PEOPLE MACHINES TICKETS SHARED SINCE
Hosting Co  Shop Owner real-admin@test.local 1 0 0 0 Sep 26, 2026
Attacker Shop yours  Mallory boss@test.local 1 0 0 0 Sep 26, 2026
Add a company ...
```
verifier_notes: confirmed: The claim matches the code. signup/page.tsx:36-40 and createShopWithOwner (src/lib/shops.ts:36-64) only check that the email is unused; neither checks isPlatformAdmin. The only reservation guard is in addUser (settings.ts:106), added in round 1, so that fix is incomplete. createCompany and the partners set-up form are already gated by requirePlatformAdmin / isPlatformAdmin, which leaves /signup as the one bypass. Admin rights come purely from the email (session.ts:43-58), so whoever signs up with the address becomes platform admin. That gives them the /companies list with every owner's name and email, company creation, the install-wide hub join/leave (hub.ts:26,46 requireInstallAdmin; also partners.ts:55) and deletion of shared posts. Two preconditions hold it at medium rather than critical: ALLOW_SIGNUP=true (INSTALL.md says leave it unset; the Windows program only opens sign-up with SETUP_TOKEN for its first company) and a listed admin address that nobody has claimed yet. The documented setup seeds SEED_OWNER_EMAIL, which normally is the admin address.

title: Login pacing is checked before the failure is recorded, so a burst of parallel wrong passwords skips pacing entirely
description: paced() reads the per-account failure count when a request arrives (`const n = count(`e:${email}`); if (n < 5) return fn();`). The count only goes up in fail(), after the bcrypt compare finishes (bcryptjs, cost 10, async). Every request that arrives while fewer than 5 failures are recorded runs straight away and in parallel, however many there are. The per-address limit (`if (ip && count(`i:${ip}`) >= 50) return null`, line 79) has the same check-then-act gap. The window also resets 15 minutes after the first failure (count() compares against `since`), so the same burst works again every window. The round-2 fix ('pacing per account instead of a lockout') is therefore incomplete: the number of guesses per window is limited by server CPU, not by the policy of 5 free tries followed by growing waits.
failure_scenario: Hosted app, target account owner@shop. Many sign-in attempts for that email arrive at once through /api/auth/callback/credentials or the login action. All of them see n=0 because none has recorded a failure yet, so all are checked right away instead of 5 followed by 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... 30 s waits. Without TRUST_PROXY there is no per-address cap at all, and with it the cap has the same gap.
suggested_fix: Reserve the slot before doing the work: count the attempt at entry (for example an in-flight counter per email and per address, added to count() in the decision) and release it on success. Or send every attempt for an email through the per-email queue, not just those after 5 failures, and cap in-flight attempts per email at 1. Use a sliding or decaying window instead of a reset 15 minutes after the first failure.
verifier_notes: confirmed: paced() reads count(`e:${email}`) when a request arrives, and fail() only records a failure after the async bcrypt.compare finishes (src/auth.ts:50-51, 80-86). Every attempt that arrives before 5 failures are recorded runs straight away and in parallel. The per-address check at line 79 has the same check-then-act gap and only applies with TRUST_PROXY. The window is fixed at 15 minutes from the first failure (line 25), so the burst can be repeated every window. The round-2 pacing is meant to allow 5 free tries, then one at a time with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... up to 30 s waits and at most 20 queued. Parallel requests skip all of that, so the guess rate is limited only by server CPU for bcrypt. The rate stays bounded by bcrypt cost and passwords are 8+ characters, so medium, not high.

title: Reserved platform-admin emails can be claimed through /signup (the reservation only exists in addUser)
description: Round 1 added a reservation so nobody else can take an address in PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS (src/actions/settings.ts:105-106). It lives only in addUser. createShopWithOwner, used by /signup, has no such check, and neither does the signup action (src/app/signup/page.tsx:33-40). isPlatformAdmin() is decided purely by the account's email, so whoever registers a listed address first gets the Companies screen (every company's owner, email and counts, plus creating companies), install-admin rights over the hub connection (requireInstallAdmin), and the right to delete any company's shared notes (src/actions/shared.ts:54, src/actions/hub.ts:153).
failure_scenario: The operator sets PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS=me@ops.com,partner@ops.com with ALLOW_SIGNUP=true, and partner@ops.com hasn't signed in or been created yet (or an address is listed ahead of time). An anonymous visitor signs up at /signup with email partner@ops.com. On their first page load the nav shows Companies, and they can join or leave the install's hub and add companies.
suggested_fix: Put the reservation in createShopWithOwner, taking the caller's platform-admin status (allowed only when a platform admin creates it through createCompany or setUpSewingShop). Or refuse any isPlatformAdmin(email) in the signup action. Better still, tie platform-admin status to a flag on the user row set by seeding or the operator, not to a bare email string.
evidence:
src/actions/settings.ts:105-106: `// The StitchBench administrator's address carries install-wide rights: nobody else may take it for a login.\n if (isPlatformAdmin(email) && !isPlatformAdmin(admin.email)) throw new UserError("That email is reserved on this StitchBench.");`
src/lib/shops.ts:40-46 (createShopWithOwner): only checks fields and `if (await db.user.findUnique({ where: { email } }))` with no isPlatformAdmin check.
src/lib/session.ts:43-46 / 53-55: platform and install admin rights come from isPlatformAdmin(u.email).
Found by code reading.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The round-1 reservation exists only in addUser (src/actions/settings.ts:105-106). createShopWithOwner (src/lib/shops.ts:36-63) and the signup action (src/app/signup/page.tsx:31-40) never call isPlatformAdmin. Signup also never verifies that the person owns the email. Platform-admin and install-admin rights come from the email string alone (session.ts:45, 55, 64), so anyone who registers a listed but not-yet-registered address through /signup becomes StitchBench administrator. That means the Companies screen with every owner's email, creating companies, joining and leaving the hub, and deleting any shared note. The round-1 fix is incomplete. Impact depends on a listed address not being registered yet (for example a second admin listed ahead of time, or the window between deploy and the operator's own sign-up), so medium.

title: Restoring a backup made before a program update leaves the older specs and factory settings in place for good
description: restore() truncates and reloads the REFERENCE tables (TensionSpec, FactorySetting, LibraryDoc) from the backup. reference.mjs decides whether to reload the shipped set by comparing the table comment (`seed:<hash>`) with the shipped file's hash. TRUNCATE doesn't touch table comments, so after a restore the comment still says the new set is loaded while the rows are the backup's older set. Every later start then skips loading, until an update ships a different seed file.
failure_scenario: The shop updates to a version with corrected tension specs or factory settings (loaded at start, comment = new hash). Later the owner restores last month's backup, or moves to a new PC and restores. The old values and labels come back, settings added in the update disappear, and ticket readings keyed by those new ids lose their labels. Restarting the program doesn't fix it, and nothing warns the owner.
suggested_fix: In restore(), for each REFERENCE table that is loaded from the backup, run `COMMENT ON TABLE ... IS NULL` inside the same transaction, so the next start reloads the shipped set. Alternatively, don't restore TensionSpec, FactorySetting or LibraryDoc (the program ships them); restore only FigureImage and ModelImage, which don't ship. main.mjs could also call loadReference right after a restore.
evidence:
Isolated run of copies of desktop/backup.mjs and reference.mjs against my own DB (scratchpad/agents/sec-files-lib/iso/ref-restore.mjs):
program 1.4 start (seed v1): [{"id":"fs-sec-1","label":"v1 label"}] comment=seed:636f37580a5cdd12
program 1.5 start (seed v2): [{"id":"fs-sec-1","label":"v2 corrected label"},{"id":"fs-sec-2","label":"v2 new setting"}] comment=seed:6a568818e64b31c9
after restoring the 1.4 backup: [{"id":"fs-sec-1","label":"v1 label"}] comment=seed:6a568818e64b31c9
next 1.5 start (seed v2 again): [{"id":"fs-sec-1","label":"v1 label"}] comment=seed:6a568818e64b31c9
Code: reference.mjs:24-25 `if (rows[0]?.c === mark) continue;`
verifier_notes: confirmed: restore() (desktop/backup.mjs:145-156) truncates and reloads TensionSpec, FactorySetting and LibraryDoc whenever the backup contains them. TRUNCATE doesn't change table comments. loadReference (reference.mjs:24-25) skips a set whose comment already equals `seed:<hash of the shipped file>`. main.mjs's restoreFromBackup restarts the server but never calls loadReference, and the startup call at main.mjs:676 is skipped because the hash matches. So a restored pre-update backup brings back the older specs and factory settings, and they stay until an update ships a different seed file. Techs silently get outdated reference values. This is a less common flow (restore after an update), so medium.
also_reported_as: qa: desktop/backup.mjs:145 Restoring an older backup silently brings back old specs and factory settings that are never reloaded afterwards

title: backupsToKeep = 0 (or any non-number) deletes every backup, including the one just made, and still reports 'Backup saved'
description: Pruning is `listBackups(root, flavor).slice(keep)` with keep taken straight from the user-editable config.json (INSTALL.md documents backupsToKeep). With 0 (a common way to write 'keep all'), null, or a non-numeric string like "all" (slice(NaN) is slice(0)), every backup of this program is deleted, including the one just written. backup() still returns its path, so the tray says 'Backup saved.' and the log says 'saved to <dir>'. Negative numbers delete the oldest backups instead of keeping any number.
failure_scenario: The owner sets "backupsToKeep": 0 in config.json, meaning unlimited. The next nightly backup deletes all 30 existing backups and then its own. Months later the disk dies and there's nothing to restore. Nothing in the tray or the log showed a problem.
suggested_fix: Validate the value: `const keep = Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? n : 30` (or treat 0 as 'never prune'), and always leave out the backup just created (`.filter(d => d !== dir)`) when pruning. Log and notify when the setting is invalid.
evidence:
Same isolated run (my DB):
keep=0: backup() returned stitchbench-2026-09-26-17-26-25; exists afterwards: false; backups left: 0
main.mjs:407 passes `keep: cfg.backupsToKeep` unvalidated; backup-now.mjs:11 likewise.
verifier_notes: confirmed: main.mjs:149 merges config.json over the defaults with no validation. main.mjs:407 and backup-now.mjs:11 pass cfg.backupsToKeep straight to backup(). The `keep = 30` default parameter only applies when the value is undefined, so 0, null or a string like "all" reaches `listBackups(...).slice(keep)` at backup.mjs:98, and slice(0) / slice(null) / slice(NaN) deletes every backup, including the one just written. runBackup still logs 'saved to <dir>' and returns the path. It needs the owner to hand-edit config.json (backupsToKeep is documented in INSTALL.md:93), but the result is a silent loss of every backup, so medium.

title: Quit and Restart hang forever once the embedded Postgres has already exited (failed start or crash), so the program stays running with no way to close it
description: quit() does `await db?.stop()` with no timeout. embedded-postgres 17.10.0-beta.17 stop() returns early only when `this.process` is unset. Otherwise it waits for that process's 'exit' event (`this.process.on('exit', resolve)` followed by taskkill on Windows). When start() fails, the spawned postgres has already exited and emitted 'exit', but `this.process` is still set. main.mjs:206-211 swallows that failure on purpose ('trying the running one'). A postgres that dies while the program runs leaves the same state. From then on quit() never reaches app.exit(0).
failure_scenario: Case 1: postgres fails to start (port 5439 taken, disk full, antivirus) and the fallback connect fails. The 'couldn't start' dialog shows, then `return quit()` (line 673) hangs. The process keeps the single-instance lock and the tray icon, and every later launch just calls showWindow() on a dead server. Case 2: postgres crashes, or the program adopted one left running. Tray 'Quit' and 'Restart StitchBench' (app.relaunch()+quit()) do nothing. Further clicks return early because `quitting` is already true. The user has to use Task Manager.
suggested_fix: In quit(), race db.stop() against a timeout (e.g. 10 s). Skip stop() when `db.process?.exitCode != null` or start() failed; in that case clear db.process and stop an adopted server with `pg_ctl stop -D <dir> -m fast`. Always call app.exit afterwards.
evidence: stop() body copied from node_modules/embedded-postgres/dist/index.js (npm pack 17.10.0-beta.17). Simulation: a spawned process exits, start() rejects on 'close', then stop() is awaited: output `start failed (like 'trying the running one'): undefined` / `STILL WAITING after 5 s: quit() never reaches app.exit`. main.mjs:640 `await db?.stop().catch((e) => log("postgres stop:", e));`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: quit() (desktop/main.mjs:634-642) awaits db.stop() with no timeout. In embedded-postgres 17.10.0-beta.17, stop() returns early only when this.process is unset. Otherwise it attaches on('exit', resolve) and then kills the process. startDatabase() (main.mjs:206-211) swallows a start() failure on purpose. The failure is the rejection from the child's 'close' event, which fires after 'exit', so the promise returned by stop() can never resolve. This happens in the 'adopted' path the code was written for: postgres.exe is left running after the program is killed, the new spawn exits because of the postmaster.pid lock, and the program uses the old server. It also happens when the fallback connect fails (the startup-error dialog then calls quit()), and when postgres crashes during a session. In all of these, Quit and Restart hang, and the `quitting` flag makes every later click a no-op. The adopted case also repeats: killing the program in Task Manager leaves postgres running, so the next launch adopts it again.

title: Hosted installs never get corrected or new factory specs: `npm start` seeds with --if-empty and skips any table that has rows
description: `npm start` runs `release` = `prisma migrate deploy && tsx prisma/seed.ts --if-empty`. With --if-empty, `step()` returns 'already loaded' as soon as TensionSpec or FactorySetting has even one row. Rows added, changed or removed in a newer tension_specs.json or factory_settings.json are never applied to a hosted (Railway) database. README.md:107-108 says `npm start` '... loads any missing reference data before the server starts', which is not true for missing rows. The Windows program handles this properly: desktop/reference.mjs records a content hash and upserts a changed set. AGENTS.md describes spec corrections as 'regenerate prisma/seed-data/tension_specs.json ... then npm run db:seed', and no deploy path runs that for hosted shops. INSTALL.md documents no step for it either (the manual reload is only documented for the Windows program). The hub README advertises 'Data sets. Files the hub admin publishes to every shop, for example updated factory specs', but nothing in StitchBench (src/, desktop/, scripts/) ever calls /v1/datasets. That channel does not exist on the client side.
failure_scenario: The maintainer fixes a wrong upper-tension value for a model in the xlsx, regenerates tension_specs.json and ships a release. Windows-program shops get the corrected value on their next start. Every Railway-hosted shop keeps showing the old, wrong 'Factory: upper ...' range on tickets and machine pages indefinitely, and spec rows added in the release are missing.
suggested_fix: Use the same approach as desktop/reference.mjs in the release step: store a hash of each seed file (table comment or a small meta table) and upsert and prune when it changes. Or drop --if-empty for the reference tables and keep it only for seedFirstShop. Correct README.md:107. Either implement dataset pulling in src/lib/hub.ts or remove that claim from the hub README.
evidence: Own fresh DB qa_bti_a: migrate deploy, then full seed (634 specs / 14392 settings). Then `DELETE FROM "TensionSpec" ... LIMIT 5; UPDATE "FactorySetting" SET "valueMin"=999 WHERE id=<first>` and `npx tsx prisma/seed.ts --if-empty` -> `Tension specs: already loaded / Factory settings: already loaded`. Afterwards `count(*) TensionSpec = 629` and one FactorySetting still has valueMin=999. seed.ts:172-176: `if (ifEmpty && (await count()) > 0) { console.log(`${name}: already loaded`); return; }`. `grep -rni dataset src desktop scripts` -> no matches.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The claim matches the code. `npm start` runs `release`, which runs `seed.ts --if-empty`. `step()` skips TensionSpec and FactorySetting entirely once either table has any rows, so a changed, added or removed spec row in a new release never reaches a hosted database. The upsert/prune code in seedSpecs and seedSettings is never reached on hosted. The Windows program gets these updates through desktop/reference.mjs, whose header says 'Same result as npm run db:seed', so the two install modes behave differently. README.md says `npm start` 'loads any missing reference data', which is misleading. No client code uses the hub's data sets.
